chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who marries five (women) in one marriage tie, he (peace be upon him) said: He frees the way (divorces) whichever one he desires, and keeps the four.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man marries five women in one contract?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism for managing polygyny when a man contracts five wives in a single 'aqd' (marriage tie), ruling that he retains the right to choose which one to release to maintain the limit of four. It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the structure of marriage contracts, distinguishing between simultaneous entry and sequential addition. The ruling underscores the principle that the maximum number of concurrent wives is four, regardless of how the initial contracts were structured.
